en: The Sūtra on King Ajātaśatru’s Inquiry Regarding the Five Heinous Crimes, translated by the Śramaṇa Dharmajñāna of the Western Jin Dynasty.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Bhagavān was staying at Vulture Peak Mountain in the city of Rājagṛha, together with...
There was a great assembly of five hundred bhikṣus.
Devadatta went to the place where King Ajātaśatru was; having arrived, he took his seat.
Then King Ajātaśatru rose from his seat, prostrated himself with his head at Devadatta’s feet, and returned to his seat.
Then King Ajātaśatru said to Devadatta:
"I have heard, Venerable Devadatta,
that the śramaṇa Gautama often says this:"

“There are five heinous crimes (*ānantarya-karma*). If a son of good family or a daughter of good family commits these five unforgivable offenses, they will certainly enter hell without doubt. What are the five?
[The text continues with the enumeration of the five.]”
That is to say: killing one's father, killing one's mother, harming an Arhat, causing schism in the Sangha, and harboring malice toward the Tathāgata.
These five unforgivable offenses—if any man or woman commits such acts, they will certainly enter hell without doubt.
“Devadatta! If I have now personally killed my father, the King, shall I too enter hell?
At that time, Devadatta said to King Ajātaśatru:
“Great King! Do not harbor fear; what calamity could there be?
What fault could there be?”
Who commits a transgression and receives its retribution?
Who creates a transgression and must undergo its fruit?
Yet, Great King, you have committed no evil or rebellious act; he who commits evil shall himself receive the retribution.
At that time, a great number of bhikṣus, having dressed in their robes and taken up their bowls at the proper hour, entered the city of Rājagṛha for alms.
While these many bhikṣus were entering the city of Rājagṛha for alms, they heard King Ajātaśatru say to Devadatta:
"Venerable Devadatta!"
I have heard the Śramaṇa Gautama say this:
"There are five unforgivable offenses; if any man or woman commits these five deeds, they will certainly enter hell without doubt."
"I have killed my father, the King, with my own hands despite being innocent;
shall I not fall into hell? Then Devadatta replied, "Do not fear, Great King!"
Who commits misfortune, and from what does that misfortune arise?
Who commits evil and subsequently receives retribution?
The King does not commit misfortune; he who commits misfortune shall himself receive the retribution.

Then, after the many bhikṣus had finished their almsround in the city of Rājagṛha, they gathered up their robes and bowls following their meal, placed their sitting mats (niṣīdana) over their shoulders, and went to where the World-Honored One was. Prostrating themselves with their heads at his feet, they sat to one side and related in detail to the World-Honored One the discussion they had held with King Ajātaśatru.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke this verse:
"The fool knows this state, Claiming that transgressions bring no retribution.
But as I now observe the future, The experience of retribution has its fixed place."
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the bhikṣus:
"That King Ajātaśatru of Magadha, though he has killed his father the king, shall before long come to my presence and shall develop equal faith in me;
yet after his life ends, he shall fall into hell like a struck ball."
At that time, a certain bhikṣu addressed the Blessed One, saying:
“When his life there in that niraya has ended, where will he be reborn?
The Blessed One replied:
"Having passed away from that niraya, you shall be reborn in the realm of the Four Great Kings.
The bhikṣu addressed him, saying,
"After passing away from there, where will I be reborn?"
The World-Honored One told him:
"Bhikṣu! Having passed away from there, you shall be reborn in the Heaven of the Thirty-three."
The bhikṣu addressed the Buddha, saying:
“Having passed away from the Heaven of the Thirty-three, where will he be reborn?
The World-Honored One replied:
“Bhikṣu! Having passed away from the Heaven of the Thirty-three, you shall be reborn in the Yāma Heaven.
The bhikṣu addressed [the Buddha], saying:
“World-Honored One!
After passing away from that life, where will they be reborn?
The World-Honored One replied:
"Having passed away from the Yāma Heaven, one shall be reborn in the Tuṣita Heaven.
The bhikṣu addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
"When his life ends in Tuṣita Heaven, where will he be reborn?
The World-Honored One replied,
"When his life ends in Tuṣita Heaven, he shall be reborn in the Nirmāṇarati Heaven."
The bhikṣu said to the Buddha:
“Having passed away from the Heaven of Mastery over Transformations (Nirmāṇarati), where will he be reborn?
The World-Honored One replied:
“Monks! Having passed away from the Heaven of Mastery over Others' Emanations, one shall be reborn in the Heaven of Making Use of Others' Emanations.
The monks addressed [the Buddha], saying:
“World-Honored One!
Having passed away from the Heaven of Making Use of Others' Transformations, where will he be reborn?
The World-Honored One replied:

“Monks! Having passed away from the Heaven of Making Use of Others’ Emanations (Paranirmita-vaśavartin), one will be reborn in the Heaven of Delighting in Emanations (Nirmāṇarati), the Tuṣita Heaven, the Yāma Heaven, the Heaven of the Thirty-three (Trāyastriṃśa), or the Heaven of the Four Great Kings (Cāturmahārājika); thereafter, one shall again be born among human beings.”
The bhikṣu said to the Buddha:
“World-Honored One!
When my life here comes to an end, where shall I be reborn?”
The World-Honored One said:

"Bhikṣus! King Ajātaśatru of Magadha shall not fall into the three evil realms for twenty kalpas. He will transmigrate among gods and humans, and finally, taking his last body, he will shave off his hair and beard, don the three dharma robes, and with firm faith leave the household life to study the Way. He shall become a pratyekabuddha named Vimala."
The bhikṣu said: "How extraordinary!
How marvelous!"
“World-Honored One!
Having committed such calamities and transgressions, he yet experienced such joy and became a pratyekabuddha named ‘The Stainless’.
The World-Honored One replied:
“King Ajātaśatru of Magadha has accomplished his resolve, and all manner of goodness has arrived for him.
Monks! One who is capable of accomplishing their resolve can attain the ground of deliverance from hell.”

"If the aspiration has been formed but not accomplished, yet the causal conditions have been fulfilled, although one has not yet been born in hell, it is still possible to employ skillful means so as not to reach hell.
The bhikṣu said: "If that person has accomplished both matters, where will they be reborn?"
The World-Honored One said:
"When those two conditions are fulfilled, one will be reborn in two places. What are these two?"
“[They will be born] among gods and humans. The bhikṣu said:
“Regarding those whose resolve is accomplished but whose conditions are not accomplished—what is the difference between these two matters?”
The World-Honored One said:
"Bhikṣu! When the aspiration is accomplished but the causal conditions are not accomplished, this is the copper-root."
“Bhikṣu! One whose resolve is not yet perfected but whose causal conditions are perfected—this one possesses sharp faculties. The bhikṣu said:
“What is the distinction between those of dull faculties and those of sharp faculties?
The Blessed One replied:
“O bhikṣus, as for those of dull faculties—”
— those who do not progress;
those of keen faculties— monks!— are clever and wise.
The bhikṣu said: “What is the difference between these two?
To which karma should one return?”
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke these verses:
"Wisdom is supreme in the world; one should proceed to the place of peace.
Those who can understand all equal karmas will sever birth, existence, and death."
“Thus it is, bhikṣu! There is this distinction.

At that time, having heard what the Buddha had spoken, that bhikṣu rejoiced and practiced accordingly; he then rose from his seat, prostrated with his head at the Buddha’s feet, circumambulated him three times, and withdrew.
At that time, on that very day, the bhikṣu dressed himself, took up his bowl, and entered the city of Rājagṛha to beg for food, proceeding to the gate of the palace of King Māgadha.
At that time, King Ajātaśatru saw the bhikṣu approaching from afar; having seen him, he immediately commanded his gatekeepers:
"Gatekeepers, what is this?
I have already given orders that no Śākya bhikṣus are to be admitted here, with the exception of the Venerable Devadatta."
Then the gatekeeper seized the bhikṣu by the hand and drove him out through the gate.
At that time, the bhikṣu raised his right hand and said to the King of Magadha:
"I am Your Majesty’s great spiritual friend; I am a place of peace and security, free from all afflictions."
Then the king replied, "How so,
bhikṣu? For what reason do you say such things as, 'I am the Great King's good friend' and 'I am a place of security'?"
Then that bhikṣu said to King Ajātaśatru: "The World-Honored One spoke concerning the king, saying:
'Although the King of Magadha has killed his father, the king, once he has completed his life through such evil deeds, he shall be reborn in hell like a ball being struck.'"
When their life there ends, they shall be born in the palace of the Four Great Kings;
when their life there ends, they shall be born in the Heaven of the Thirty-three;
when their life there ends, they shall be born in the Yāma Heaven, the Tuṣita Heaven, the Nirmāṇarati Heaven, and the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven.

When their life there comes to an end, they shall again be reborn in the Heaven of Mastery over Transformations, the Tuṣita Heaven, the Yāma Heaven, the Heaven of the Thirty-three, and the palaces of the Four Great Kings;
thereafter, they shall be born here among humans and receive a human form.

"In this way, Great King, for twenty kalpas you shall not fall into the three evil realms. Wandering through the human world, you will finally receive a human body; you shall shave off your hair and beard, don the three dharma robes, and with firm faith leave the household life to study the Way, becoming a pratyekabuddha named 'The Stainless'."
"The reason for this, Great King, is that you shall attain such rootless faith.
Having spoken these words, the bhikṣu withdrew and departed.
At that time, King Ajātaśatru, having heard what that bhikṣu had said, was neither joyful nor angry; nor did he accept what was said. He then addressed Prince Jīvaka, saying: "Jīvaka!..."
A śramaṇa came to me and spoke these words:

"That Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha has granted him a prediction; having killed his father, the king, he committed such an evil and rebellious act that after his life ends, he shall be reborn in hell like a struck ball."

When their life there ends, they shall be reborn in the Heaven of the Four Great Kings, the Heaven of the Thirty-three, the Yāma Heaven, the Tuṣita Heaven, the Nirmāṇarati Heaven, and the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven;

when their life there ends, they shall again be reborn in the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven, the Tuṣita Heaven, the Yāma Heaven, the Heaven of the Thirty-three, and the palaces of the Four Great Kings;
when their life there ends, they shall be reborn among humans.
In his final birth as a human, he shaved off his hair and beard, donned the three dharma robes, and with firm faith left the household life to study the Way, becoming a pratyekabuddha named Vimala.
"Go, Jīvaka! To that ascetic Gautama and inquire whether such words were truly spoken. He replied:

"So be it, Great King! Then Prince Jīvaka, having received the command of the King of Magadha, departed from the city of Rājagṛha and went to Vulture Peak Mountain to the place where the World-Honored One was.
Having arrived, he prostrated with his head at [the Buddha’s] feet and sat to one side.
Then Prince Jīvaka related to the Tathāgata, in full detail, the instructions spoken by the King of Magadha.
The World-Honored One said:
"It is so, Jīvaka! The words of the Buddha, the World-Honored One, are not twofold; what he speaks accords with the facts."
Why is this so? Jīvaka! That King Ajātaśatru shall establish rootless faith.
"Jīvaka! All those who are men or women shall likewise have this destiny, without exception.
When Prince Jīvaka had received these instructions from the Tathāgata, he immediately rose from his seat, prostrated himself with his head at the Buddha's feet, and then withdrew.
He went to the place where King Ajātaśatru of Magadha was, and having arrived, he spoke to the king, saying:
"That Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha has indeed spoken these words."
Why is this so? Because all those who have attained rootless faith are without distinction.
I pray that Your Majesty will go to where that Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, resides.
The king replied, “Jīvaka!

I have heard that the śramaṇa Gautama possesses such incantations and arts that he can subdue the people and cause all the heterodox followers of other teachings to accept his instruction. For this reason, I am not able to go and see the śramaṇa Gautama.”
Wait, Jīvaka! I shall first examine whether that śramaṇa Gautama possesses omniscience;
only if he truly possesses omniscience will I go to see that śramaṇa Gautama.

At that time, Prince Jīvaka, having heard these words from the King of Magadha, departed from the city of Rājagṛha and went to Vulture Peak Mountain, arriving at the place where the World-Honored One was.
Having arrived, he prostrated with his head at [the Buddha's] feet, sat to one side, and reported this matter to the World-Honored One.
At that time, the World-Honored One said: "Jīvaka!
"The King of Magadha will come to me before long and shall attain rootless faith; even after my entry into parinirvāṇa, he shall make offerings to my relics."
Prince Jīvaka was filled with joy and leaped for gladness, unable to contain himself.
Then the World-Honored One expounded the subtle and wondrous Dharma to Prince Jīvaka, causing him to give rise to great joy.

At that time, Prince Jīvaka, having heard this profound Dharma from the Tathāgata, immediately rose from his seat, prostrated himself with his head at the Buddha’s feet, circumambulated him three times, and then withdrew.
At that time, Prince Jīvaka, having heard what the Buddha had spoken, rejoiced and practiced accordingly.
*The Sūtra on King Ajātaśatru’s Inquiry Regarding the Five Heinous Offenses*.
